content.comment_body: I'm using [product_name] [product_name]. When I select 'keep me logged on' in my web browser, it doesn't seem to work. Is there a solution for this?
Please provide more details. Which [product_name] do you have specifically? Also, share the complete [article_no].
I have three separate devices in my network: 1x [company_name] [product_name] 12/24V basis display [article_no], and 2x [company_name] [product_name] 230V AC basis [article_no].
On which [product_name] are you experiencing this issue? Is it just one, or all three?
I'm experiencing this issue on all three devices, both from my smartphone and computer.
Are all the devices on the same IP network segment?
Yes, they're all within subnet 255.255.255.0.
I'm referring to the IP subnet itself, not just the subnet mask.
Yes, all the devices are in the same network. Is that what you meant?
An IP address contains four segments: aaa.bbb.ccc.ddd. The first three segments (aaa.bbb.ccc) define the subnet, and ddd is the device's unique address within that subnet.
Thank you for explaining. Yes, all my devices share the same subnet (192.168.1.xxx).
That's only the case for class C networks. Still, the original poster uses a class C network mask (255.255.255.0), so your suggestion is correct.
Why is the 'keep me logged on' option not working in the browser?
If I knew the answer, I would have already posted it.
Maybe a simple check: Did you enable the web server in the access control settings?
Could there be another bug with [version_no] hardware? No matter if 'Keep me logged on' is active, after closing and reopening the web browser, the device always requests login credentials.
Could cookies be causing the problem? The manual notes: 'Make sure you do not disable cookies on your browser.'
I hope this issue gets fixed – it's inconvenient having to log in every time.
Yes, I've enabled the web server in the access control.

I hope this gets fixed soon – having to log in repeatedly is frustrating. It isn't a bug in the [product_name] [version_no] hardware. You also have two [product_name] [version_no] units. [article_no] = [product_name] [version_no] with display. [article_no] = [product_name] [version_no] without display. I also have one [product_name] [version_no] (12/24RCE) and two [product_name] [version_no] (also 12/24RCE). None of mine have this problem.
I have cookies enabled. Could cookies still be related to the issue? The manual says: 'Make sure you do not disable cookies on your browser.'
'Keep me logged on' works for me, so it may be a browser-specific issue. However, since others have reported this too, I've forwarded it to development.

I use [product_name] [version_no] with Chrome browser. After logging in and selecting 'keep me logged on,' I navigate the pages and close the browser without logging out. When I reopen the browser, the home page loads without asking for login credentials. The feature works fine for me.
Thanks for your help!

What I have: Device Series [product_name][version_no] [article_no], Device Type [article_no] Firmware Version 1.82.02: login works fine. Device Series [product_name][version_no] [article_no], Device Type [article_no] Firmware Version 1.82.02: login fails. Device Series [product_name][version_no] [article_no], Device Type [article_no] Firmware Version 1.83.01: login fails.

[article_no] = [product_name] [version_no] (Firmware V1.83.01). [article_no] = [product_name] [version_no] (Firmware V1.82.x). If the webserver shows [article_no] for a [product_name] [version_no] (Firmware V1.83.01), that's not correct. Attached is a brief history of [article_no] devices.

analysis.insight_summary: The main user concern is that the 'keep me logged on' feature in the [product_name] [product_name] web interface is not functioning properly across different devices, including both smartphones and computers. Despite troubleshooting and checking settings such as cookies and web server access control, no reliable fix or workaround has been identified in the discussion, leaving users with inconsistent or disabled persistent login functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the 'keep me logged on' feature in the [product_name] web editor to function consistently, allowing them to stay logged in across sessions without repeated authentication.
